resolutions.evidence: Regression TestExecuteWorktreeSetupFailureReportsOnlyExistingArtifacts. RED: go test ./workflow -run '^TestExecuteWorktreeSetupFailureReportsOnlyExistingArtifacts$' -count=1 failed because Worktree named a nonexistent path. GREEN: the same command passed after creating the log before setup, recording setup failure there, and assigning Worktree only after git worktree add succeeds.

Regressions TestExecuteReportsIntegrationCancellationWithoutCallingItAConflict and TestExecuteReportsIntegrationHookFailureWithoutCallingItAConflict, with the existing conflict test strengthened. RED: the cancellation regression failed with 'workflow: integration conflict ... context canceled'. GREEN: targeted tests passed after cancellation was reported with its context error, true conflicts were identified by unmerged paths, and other merge failures were reported as operational failures.

Windows regressions TestWindowsTaskkillCommandTargetsProcessTree and TestRunTaskCommandCancelsNestedProcessTreeWindows. RED: GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go test -c -o /tmp/godog-workflow-windows-red.exe ./workflow failed with undefined newTaskkillCommand. GREEN: the Windows test binary cross-compiled after adding a Windows-specific taskkill.exe /T /F /PID implementation; the behavioral regression exercises a real parent and descendant when run on Windows. The Darwin runner cannot execute the Windows binary, while existing Unix descendant cancellation remains covered locally.
